Where it began

Jofra Archer was born in Bridgetown, Barbados, on 1 April 1995, and went to Christ Church Foundation School near Oistins. He played three times for the West Indies Under-19 side in 2014, then moved to England the following year.

Sussex gave him his first-class debut in July 2016, in a match against the touring Pakistanis, and his first one-day game for them came later that month. It did not take long for word to spread. Franchise teams around the world wanted him, from the Hobart Hurricanes in the Big Bash to the Rajasthan Royals in the IPL, where he was player of the match on his debut in 2018. That summer he also finished a T20 Blast game against Middlesex with a hat-trick in the final over.

The player

His first England caps came in May 2019, and within weeks he was at the heart of their World Cup. He played every match of the tournament, and when the final against New Zealand ended level, England gave him the ball for the super over. They won the cup, and the ICC named him in its team of the tournament.

Test cricket followed straight away. In the 2019 Ashes his first wicket was Cameron Bancroft, and in the next Test he took 6 for 45 as Australia were bowled out for 179. Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2020. By October 2026 he had played 23 Tests from 2019, taking 83 wickets at 28.64, with four five-wicket hauls. After almost four years away from the Test side he returned for the Lord's Test against India in 2025.

What made him special

Real speed, and the skill to use it at both ends of an innings. After the 2019 World Cup the ICC picked out his work with the new ball and in the closing overs alike. In the IPL of 2020 he was named Most Valuable Player even though his team finished bottom, which says a good deal about how much he gave them.

With the bat he was more of a cameo artist. His 364 Test runs include one fifty, a reminder to his team-mates that he had been watching them closely.

Away from the middle

White-ball cricket brought plenty of good days. In July 2026 he was player of the match in a T20 against India, taking 3 for 29 as England won by 125 runs and bowled India out for 76. Away from cricket, his football team is Manchester United.

And finally

He was born on the first of April, though there was never anything to laugh about in facing him. England's own batsmen, who met him only in the nets, were the lucky ones.
